mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to low discount rates and accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.5% occurs in 10% of observations but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% within 3 months signals monetary tightening, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors price in higher discount rates.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 0.5% within 3 months occurs in 10% of observations but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate labor market tightening and inflationary pressure, predicting negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise >0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise >0.5% in 1 month occurs in 10% of observations but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a demand expansion cycle, rising housing starts (HOUST) and residential sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both rise >0.5% in 1 month occurs in 10% of observations but 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A supply contraction indicated by INDPRO below 100 consistently predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced economic activity and lower corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: INDPRO below 100 occurs in 10% of observations but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1700 within 1 month signals weak consumer demand, predicting negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: HOUST below 1700 within 1 month occurs in 10% of observations but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 265 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 0.5%, it indicates an inflationary shock without monetary policy response, predicting negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL above 265 and FEDFUNDS below 0.5% occurs in 10% of observations but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime (indicated by falling INDPRO and rising UNRATE), the signal predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced economic output and increased recession risk.
failure_condition: INDPRO falling and UNRATE rising occurs in 10% of observations but 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of those instances.
